Create a Likert chart

Source: R/likert_chart.R
likert_chart.Rd

Draws the answers to survey questions on an ordered scale (from "Strongly disagree" to "Strongly agree", from "Very bad" to "Very good", ...) as diverging stacked bars: the negative answers go to the left of a centre line and the positive ones to the right, with a neutral answer (the middle level of an odd scale) split across the line. The share of negative and positive answers is written at both ends of each bar.

Usage

likert_chart(
  data,
  question,
  response,
  value = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  colors = NULL,
  sort = c("none", "positive", "negative"),
  show_values = TRUE,
  show_totals = TRUE,
  bar_height = 0.7,
  label_font_size = 11,
  legend = TRUE,
  legend_font_size = 11,
  hover = TRUE,
  animate = TRUE,
  title = NULL,
  title_font_size = 16,
  font = "Verdana, Geneva, Tahoma, sans-serif",
  bg_col = "white",
  text_col = "#333333",
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, with one row per answer (or one row per question and answer with a value column of counts).

question

The name of the column with the questions (or items).

response

The name of the column with the answers.

value

Optional. The name of a numeric column of counts. When NULL, each row counts as one answer.

levels

Optional. The answers in order, from the most negative to the most positive. Defaults to the factor levels of response, or to the order of appearance.

colors

Optional. One colour per level. By default a red - grey - blue scale.

sort

How to order the questions: "none" (the default), "positive" (the most positive at the top) or "negative".

show_values

Logical. Write the share of each answer in its segment when it fits. Defaults to TRUE.

show_totals

Logical. Write the share of negative and positive answers at the ends of each bar. Defaults to TRUE.

bar_height

The height of the bars as a share of the space of each question. Defaults to 0.7.

label_font_size

The font size of the questions. Defaults to 11.

legend

Logical. Show the legend. Defaults to TRUE.

legend_font_size

The font size of the legend. Defaults to 11.

hover

Logical. Show tooltips and highlight on hover. Defaults to TRUE.

animate

Logical. Grow the bars when the chart is drawn. Defaults to TRUE.

title

Optional. The title of the chart.

title_font_size

The font size of the title. Defaults to 16.

font

The font family. Defaults to "Verdana, Geneva, Tahoma, sans-serif".

bg_col

The background colour. Defaults to "white".

text_col

The colour of the text. Defaults to "#333333".

width, height

Optional. The size of the chart.

Value

An r2d3 htmlwidget.

Interactions

Hover a segment to see its share and count, while the same answer is highlighted for every question; hover the legend to highlight an answer. The bars grow from the centre line when the chart is drawn. Inside Shiny, clicking a segment sets input$<id>_clicked to a list with question, response, count and percent.

Examples

survey <- data.frame(
  question = rep(c("The product is easy to use", "Support answers quickly",
                   "The price is fair", "I would recommend it"), each = 5),
  answer = rep(c("Strongly disagree", "Disagree", "Neutral", "Agree",
                 "Strongly agree"), times = 4),
  n = c(4, 10, 18, 45, 23,  12, 20, 25, 28, 15,  20, 30, 22, 20, 8,
        5, 8, 15, 40, 32)
)
likert_chart(survey, question = "question", response = "answer", value = "n",
             sort = "positive", title = "Customer survey")



# One row per answer, a four-point scale without a neutral answer
set.seed(1)
scale4 <- c("Never", "Rarely", "Often", "Always")
habits <- data.frame(
  habit = rep(c("Cook at home", "Walk to work", "Read before bed"), each = 60),
  answer = c(sample(scale4, 60, TRUE, c(1, 2, 4, 3)),
             sample(scale4, 60, TRUE, c(4, 3, 2, 1)),
             sample(scale4, 60, TRUE, c(2, 3, 3, 2)))
)
likert_chart(habits, question = "habit", response = "answer", levels = scale4,
             colors = c("#d6402b", "#ffb15c", "#6cc5b0", "#1f7a63"))
